look_here_first: Touch and inspect the stem and leaves first: rough goldenrod is genuinely scabrous, with short stiff hairs on the stem and rough leaf surfaces. Then compare the broader lower leaves, rapid reduction upward, and the compact terminal panicle.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: stem conspicuously rough or hispid with stiff short hairs

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: foliage distinctly scabrous to the touch

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: lower leaves broader and larger, with upper leaves abruptly smaller

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: terminal compact paniclelike array of many small yellow heads

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: typical of calcareous rocky openings, prairies, and dry woods

lookalikes.differences: Solidago radula is the rough/scabrous one: stiff stem and leaf hairs are more tactile and obvious than the fine gray pubescence of S. nemoralis. Its flowering array is generally more compact and terminal.
